result:
Round 265 (SABA-B-11c stage 1) is implemented. Typecheck, lint, Biome on my files and the 10 targeted test files (166 tests) all pass, and no STOP condition was hit. Nothing is committed. Browser acceptance is still C's job; I marked no §4 row as passed.

**What changed (9 granted files + 2 new, nothing else; frozen-tree check rc 0 before and after):**
- **Background drag:** a plain or Shift drag on an empty lane now makes a time selection on that lane. Snap uses the same grid and marker rule as the in-clip selection, Alt bypasses it, and the selection is bounded to 0 and the timeline length.
- **Marquee and click:** Ctrl/Cmd+drag is the old marquee, unchanged. A click under 4 px still sets the insert marker.
- **In-clip drag:** no longer stops at the clip edge; it continues to 0 or the timeline end.
- **Overlay:** a selection inside one clip still draws the in-clip overlay, so the perf contract holds. Any other single-lane selection reuses the existing `arrangement-lane-range` element, without the "all tracks" label.
- **Shortcut sheet:** two rows added, `select-area` and `select-time`.
- **New props:** `timelineSeconds` is optional on the lane and the clip, because three test files outside my grants mount those components directly.
- **Test rewrites:** SP13, UC10b and TG9 gain `ctrlKey: true`; SE8 now expects `end: 24`; SC1 gains the two ids. No assertion was removed.
- **New test file:** `background-time-selection-ui.test.tsx`, 16 tests covering BT1–BT9.
- **Doc 198:** written in Georgian; status line, template headings and cited test ids checked.

**Mutants (scratch copy outside `store/`, new file only):** M1–M4 each turn red on the rows the task names. An extra M5, for the reviewer fix below, also turns red. The failing lines are in the report.

**Code review:** the code-reviewer subagent ran and found no High issues.
- **Medium, vertical drag:** a vertical-only drag with Snap off created a zero-length selection. I fixed it so any zero-length result becomes no selection. This goes slightly beyond §2.1, which says "no selection" only when both ends snap onto one line, so I logged it as a ruling request for B.
- **Medium, missing tests:** I added rows for cancel keeping the last selection, marker snap, replacing an all-tracks selection, and the selection being cleared only once.
- The reviewer's four architecture notes are passed to B as proposals only; the main one is merging the duplicated selection logic into one shared function.

**Browser:** my own Playwright run on :5173 at both viewports (supporting data, not C evidence) matched C's expected values for BG-RANGE, BG-INTO-CLIP, BG-EMPTY-DELETE, CLIP-PAST-START, IN-CLIP-SAME, the Control half of MARQUEE-CTRL, VERTICAL and CLICK-SAME, with 0 page errors. I did not run SNAP, the Shift half of MARQUEE-CTRL, ALL-TRACKS, PLAYING, SHEET, SCREEN-BUDGET, FOCUS-SAME or G265-AUTH.

**Known gaps:**
- No test covers "a hidden grid means no snap" on the background drag.
- A vertical-only drag still counts as a drag, not a click: it clears the selection and leaves the insert marker where it was.
- An in-clip drag that starts at 0 s and goes left can still leave a zero-length selection; that path's rule is unchanged, as the task required.
- The selection can drift if the timeline is scrolled sideways mid-drag, the same as the in-clip drag already does.

The report includes the exact next checks for C.

Files are in `tmp/studio-real-loop/`:
- a-round-265.md
- a-round-265/
